deep.reconstruction:
Context: draft calculations for Riemann's 1860 memoir 'Über die Fortpflanzung ebener Luftwellen von endlicher Schwingungsweite'. The setting is one-dimensional isentropic gas flow with pressure law p = φ(ρ).

(A) Euler equations (top left). The momentum and mass equations are
  -(1/ρ) p_x = u_t + u u_x = -φ'(ρ) (log ρ)_x,
  -u_x = (log ρ)_t + u (log ρ)_x.
Riemann looks for a multiplier λ so that du + λ d log ρ is a total differential d(u + f(ρ)). Adding the mass equation times λ to the momentum equation gives the combination du + (φ'/λ) d log ρ in the convective term. Requiring λ = φ'/λ gives λ = ±√φ'(ρ). This defines
  f(ρ) = ∫ √φ'(ρ) d log ρ,
so that ∂f/∂log ρ = ρ f'(ρ) = √φ'(ρ) = c, the sound speed.

(B) Riemann invariants. Set
  u + f(ρ) = 2r,   -u + f(ρ) = 2s,
so that u = r - s and f(ρ) = r + s (he drops the factor 2 here). The system becomes
  r_t = -(u + ρf') r_x,
  s_t = -(u - ρf') s_x.

(C) Hodograph (interchange of variables). Take r, s as independent and x, t as dependent variables. Along s varying with r fixed, dx/dt = -r_t/r_x = u + c. Hence
  x_s = (u + c) t_s,   x_r = (u - c) t_r.
Cross-differentiating and subtracting (implicit step, mine) gives
  2c t_rs + (u+c)_r t_s - (u-c)_s t_r = 0.
Using u_r = 1, u_s = -1 and c_r = c_s = dc/df, this becomes
  2ρf' t_rs + (1 + dc/df)(t_r + t_s) = 0,
with dc/df = (∂²f/∂log ρ²)(∂log ρ/∂f), exactly as on the page. He then rewrites the coefficient:
  1 + dc/df = 1 + d log c/d log ρ = d log(ρ c)/d log ρ = d log(ρ² f')/d log ρ.
This is a linear second-order hyperbolic equation whose coefficients depend only on r + s.

(D) Potential w (lower left). The form
  (x - (u+c)t) dr - (x - (u-c)t) ds = dw
is exact. Check: ∂_s[x - (u+c)t] = -(u+c)_s t = (1 - dc/df) t, and ∂_r[-(x - (u-c)t)] = (u-c)_r t = (1 - dc/df) t. Also 1 - dc/df = -d log f'/d log ρ. Hence
  w_rs = -(∂log f'/∂log ρ) t = -(ρ f''/f') t.
From the definition, w_r + w_s = -2ct = -2ρf' t. Eliminating t gives the linear equation
  w_rs = (f''/(2f'^2)) (w_r + w_s).
With σ = f(ρ) = r + s he notes
  f''/f'^2 = -(d/dσ)(dρ/dσ)·(dσ/dρ) = -d log(dρ/dσ)/dσ,
so that w_rs = -½ (d log(dρ/dσ)/dσ)(w_r + w_s). This is the form on the next page and in the memoir. For p = Aρ^γ it gives w_rs = -((3-γ)/(2(γ-1)(r+s)))(w_r + w_s), an Euler–Poisson–Darboux equation.

(E) Riemann's method (right middle). For a model equation w_rs = f(r+s) w (written, then struck), he writes the start of a successive-approximation scheme:
  w = 1 + (r-r')(s-s') + ...,   w_r = ∫ f(r+s) w ds.
He then tries a series ansatz for the Riemann function:
  w = Σ (r-r')^m (s-s')^m φ_m(σ, σ').
He computes ∂_r∂_s[(r-r')^m (s-s')^m φ(r+s)] as
  (r-r')^{m-1}(s-s')^{m-1} [m² φ + m(σ-σ') φ' + (r-r')(s-s') φ''],
using (r-r') + (s-s') = σ - σ'. This aims at a recursion for the φ_m; the computation is left unfinished.

(F) Discontinuities (top right). Let v1, v2 be the gas velocities relative to the moving discontinuity ξ(t).
- Mass: v1 ρ1 = v2 ρ2.
- Momentum: (φ(ρ1) - φ(ρ2)) = (v2 - v1) v1 ρ1.
Solving gives
  v1 = √((ρ2/ρ1)(φ(ρ1)-φ(ρ2))/(ρ1-ρ2)),   v2 = √((ρ1/ρ2)(φ(ρ1)-φ(ρ2))/(ρ1-ρ2)).
The shock speed is dξ/dt = u1 + v1 = u2 + v2. He compares this with the characteristic speeds u1 + √φ'(ρ1) and u2 + √φ'(ρ2), using
  u1 - u2 = v2 - v1 = √((ρ1-ρ2)(φ1-φ2)/(ρ1ρ2)).
This gives
  (u1 + c1) - (u2 + c2) = √((ρ1-ρ2)(φ1-φ2)/(ρ1ρ2)) + √φ'(ρ1) - √φ'(ρ2).
He then considers the sign for ρ1 > ρ2, with φ'(ρ1) ≷ φ'(ρ2). This is the question of whether the shock lies between the characteristic speeds on its two sides, i.e. which discontinuities (compression vs. rarefaction) can persist.
errors: On this page w_r + w_s is written as -ρ f'(ρ) t; it should be -2ρ f'(ρ) t. Consequently w_rs = (f''/f'^2)(w_r + w_s) lacks a factor 1/2. The correct relation is w_rs = (f''/(2 f'^2))(w_r + w_s). The next page has the corrected factor (-2ψ'(σ)t and the factor 1/2).
The line ∂(x - (u - ρf')t)/∂r = -1 + ∂²f/∂log ρ² ... is garbled or incomplete. Correctly it should equal (1 - dc/df) t = -(d log f'/d log ρ) t, the same as the s-derivative of the other coefficient.

Physically, the jump conditions use only mass and momentum with the isentropic law p = φ(ρ). Energy conservation (Rankine 1870, Hugoniot 1887) is absent. This is the known flaw of Riemann's 1860 treatment, not an algebraic slip.
The series computation for the Riemann function (Σ(r-r')^m(s-s')^m φ_m) is unfinished and partly struck. The differentiation formula itself is correct.

results.what: Riemann invariants r, s = (f(ρ) ± u)/2 with f = ∫√φ' d log ρ, diagonalizing 1-D isentropic gas dynamics
results.modern_name: Riemann invariants / characteristic form of the p-system
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann 1860 (simple waves partly Earnshaw 1858/60, Poisson, Stokes)

results.what: Interchange of dependent and independent variables (x, t as functions of r, s), giving a linear equation for t
Potential w with dw = (x-(u+c)t)dr - (x-(u-c)t)ds, satisfying w_rs = -½ (d log(dρ/dσ)/dσ)(w_r + w_s), σ = r+s
results.modern_name: Riemann's linearized equation for the gas-dynamics hodograph; Euler–Poisson–Darboux equation for polytropic gas

results.what: Series ansatz w = Σ (r-r')^m (s-s')^m φ_m and iteration w = 1 + (r-r')(s-s') + ..., w_r = ∫ f w ds for the Riemann function
results.modern_name: Riemann function (Riemann's method for linear hyperbolic equations); successive approximations

results.what: Jump conditions ρ1 v1 = ρ2 v2 and φ(ρ1)-φ(ρ2) = ρ1 v1 (v2 - v1), with resulting shock speed
results.modern_name: Rankine–Hugoniot conditions (isentropic, mass and momentum only)

results.what: Comparison of shock speed with characteristic speeds u ± √φ' on both sides to decide admissible (compressive) discontinuities
results.usually_credited_to: Lax 1957 (general form); Riemann 1860 argued only compression shocks persist

deep.surprise_reason: Everything here is working material for Riemann's published 1860 Luftwellen memoir: Riemann invariants, hodograph, the w-equation, Riemann's method, and the isentropic jump conditions are all already credited to him. The explicit comparison of shock speed with characteristic speeds is a nice draft-level glimpse of an admissibility (Lax-type) consideration, but the memoir already discusses which discontinuities can occur.

transcription_corrections: Lower-left fragment '∂f(ρ)/∂log ρ² f(ρ)' is more likely '∂f(ρ)/∂log ρ² f'(ρ)', related to the preceding identity with ρ² f'(ρ).

In the first line of block (D) the struck '1+' (giving ∂(x-(u+ρf')t)/∂s = (∂²f/∂log ρ²)(∂log ρ/∂f) t ... ) should be read as corrected to (1 - dc/df)t = -(∂log f'/∂log ρ) t. The trailing 'f(r+s)' is a separate marginal note.
'= 0' on the right of the '-1 + ∂²f/∂log ρ²' line appears to be a separate fragment, not the value of that line.
Last left line: 'w_r + w_s = -ρ f'(ρ) t' is as written on the page (factor 2 missing in Riemann's own text, not a transcription error).
In the w-series line, φ_m(r'+s') should read φ_m(r+s) (argument σ = r+s) in the expanded derivative.
